prompt: Stage 3-5, level 7 (you leveled early on a 4-win streak), 55 gold, 91 HP. Your board is two 2-star 4-costs with items and it is the strongest in the lobby by a margin. The shop shows a third copy of your 4-cost tank. Nobody else is close to level 8. What do you do?

options.label: Skip the tank copy, sit at 55 and level 8 at 4-1 like everyone else
Buy the tank copy, level to 8 now (12 gold), and roll to ~30 to extend the win streak and cap early
Buy the copy but keep the gold; level and roll at 4-2

explanation:
This is the third legitimate reason to break 50: you have a board that wins now, and winning now compounds. A 4-win streak at stage 3 is worth 2 gold a round on top of interest, and every win is 0 HP lost while the lobby bleeds 8 a round against you. Reaching level 8 at 3-5, a full stage before anyone, turns your 4-cost odds from 10% to 30% while the pool is untouched by other level-8 rolldowns: the copies you find now are copies nobody else will contest. Spending 25 gold here likely buys a 2-star carry plus a stronger 8th unit and a streak that runs to 4-5. That is more gold than the interest you gave up, paid back in HP and tempo.

"Buy the copy but keep the gold" is the half-measure: it holds a pair on the bench for three rounds while you sit at 7 with a 7-unit board. Greeding interest with the strongest board in the lobby is how a 1st-place position becomes a 3rd: your lead is temporary and the interest is only 5 gold.
principle: When the board wins now, gold spent extending the win is cheaper than gold saved for later.
commonMistake: Applying the 50-gold floor to a win-streaking board. The floor protects players who are behind; it caps players who are ahead.
